definition: Caroline Uhler (born 1983) is a Swiss statistician working in the field of machine learning and applications in genomics.
details: Her research focuses on developing methods for causal inference to infer regulatory relationships from different data modalities (transcriptomic, proteomic, structural, etc.). She is a Full Professor in the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science and the Institute for Data, Systems and Society at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. In addition, she is a Core Institute Member at the Broad Institute, where she directs the Eric and Wendy Schmidt Center.

explainer.lead: Caroline Uhler is a Swiss statistician and computer scientist at MIT and the Broad Institute who builds causal machine-learning methods to understand how genes and cells are regulated.
explainer.knownFor: Causal inference and graphical models applied to genomics, and directing the Eric and Wendy Schmidt Center at the Broad Institute.

contributions.name: Causal discovery from interventions
contributions.detail: Methods that learn cause-and-effect networks from perturbation data—drugs, gene knockouts, overexpression—in single-cell biology.

contributions.name: Graphical models
contributions.detail: Theory and algorithms for Gaussian graphical models, the subject of her NSF CAREER award.

contributions.name: Machine learning for biology
contributions.detail: Combines transcriptomic, proteomic and structural data to infer regulatory relationships inside cells.

contributions.name: Eric and Wendy Schmidt Center
contributions.detail: Directs the Broad Institute centre that brings machine learning and biomedicine together.
